compiled_state.description:
Live capture (2026-08-06, reported by a second session attempting to certify c9f7-d6df-bce0-4b77): THREE byte-identical gate_error_v1 sidecars on c9f7, cause "step 'decide@then/verify' failed: completion recovery context bound exceeded", diagnostic stage=preflight, context_chars=121147, context_char_limit=100000, criteria_total=22, criteria_completed=0. The primary verifier handled the 121k context fine (it failed by LOOPING — aggregate_exception_type=RunawayToolLoopError, abort at 55 requests, distinct_ratio_window=0.5, search_files x11 — the c827 actuator working as designed); ONLY the recovery preflight refuses. A retry can never succeed: the store is append-only (no comment delete — pinned by test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py's own docstring), so the context only grows. The sole documented exit is --force-close: the exhaustion-is-not-a-verdict trap, third form (after the c827 loop burnouts and ed6d's evidence-run death).

This is the SECOND outgrowth of the flat bound: d59e raised 24,000 -> 100,000 when ticket 9fd4 (34,282 chars) was refused, with 2.4x headroom over the largest ticket then observed; c9f7 (121,092 chars = description 15,651 + 10 comments totaling 105,053, of which ONE plan-review remediation comment is 99,009) blew through it within weeks. A flat per-context bound chases a monotonically growing tail — the third raise would be no different, so the bound must derive from the actual capacity it protects.

Root cause: _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS (completion_recovery.py:68) conflates two different ceilings. (1) Physical: each evidence run must fit the context in one model window. (2) Economic: recovery re-sends the context once PER criterion, so recovery spend scales with context_chars x criteria_count; 100,000 was chosen to keep the worst case at _MAX_CRITERIA (32) x 100k = 3.2M chars. c9f7's actual recovery input (22 x 121,147 = 2.67M chars) is UNDER that already-ratified worst case — it is refused only because the per-axis split is arbitrary.

## Approach

Express the two ceilings directly in _validate_recovery_inputs (completion_recovery.py:131):

- PHYSICAL ceiling derived from the resolved verifier model's OWN context window, not a flat char constant. The model-window table exists today as plan_review/sizing.MODEL_LADDER (sizing.py:99-103), but its accessor largest_window_tokens (sizing.py:137) has plan-review-specific ESCALATION semantics — it returns the max window at-or-above the resolved rung because plan-review escalates models up the ladder. Completion does not escalate, so reusing that accessor would over-admit context (haiku's own window is 200k tokens; its escalation max is 1M). Move the window TABLE to model_classes.py (the shared model-knowledge module, 456 LOC — room under the 800 cap) and add an own-window accessor there: substring rung match exactly like today's, returning the matched model's OWN window, with the ladder MINIMUM for a model the ladder cannot locate (the same conservative default largest_window_tokens adopted in bug 48b3 — under-admitting is loud and recoverable, over-admitting fails mid-run). plan_review/sizing.py re-exports the table so its call sites are unchanged (the established pattern: sizing.py already re-exports review_kernel chunking constants for historical call sites). The completion char ceiling = own_window_tokens x 2 chars/token — deliberately conservative (English prose averages ~4 chars/token, so 2 chars/token halves the admitted volume) leaving the other half of the window for the system prompt, criteria (up to _MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS = 32,000), tool traffic, and output. For the default claude-sonnet-4-6 verifier (own window 1,000,000 tokens per MODEL_LADDER, sizing.py:99-103) that is 2,000,000 chars — c9f7's 121,147 fits with ~16.5x headroom; for the haiku rung (own window 200,000 tokens) the ceiling is 400,000 chars. Either way the ceiling now moves with the configured model instead of chasing the tail by hand, and the economic ceiling below remains the binding bound for realistic shapes.
- ECONOMIC ceiling: add _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS = 3_200_000 and refuse when len(context) * len(criteria) exceeds it — byte-identical to the previously ratified worst case (32 x 100k), now allocated where real tickets need it instead of split per-axis. This ceiling is EXPLICITLY INTERIM: it models the per-criterion fan-out that the banked-verification sibling (2948-48e5-666f-4677) deletes; that sibling replaces the multiplier with successor_batches (ceil(remainder/batch_cap)), shrinking the product by ~8x. Shipping the interim bound now is what unblocks re-certifications refused at preflight today.
- Refusal stays elision-free and visible, with diagnostic {context_chars, context_char_limit, criteria_total, recovery_input_chars, recovery_input_char_limit}.
- d59e's pinned invariants are preserved: nothing is ever elided (the full context reaches the model byte-identical), the criteria budget (32,000) stays <= the context budget, and an over-budget payload still refuses with zero billable calls.

Sequencing note (operator-surfaced decision): closing c9f7 after this ticket but before 2948 lands would run the operator-ruled-unapproved fan-out once (~2.67M chars, 22 evidence runs). Default: this ticket unblocks re-certification generally, but c9f7's own close waits for 2948 unless the operator explicitly accepts one fan-out run; recorded here so the close is a deliberate call, not a side effect.

Out of scope, filed separately: write-time comment-size hygiene (the 99k scanner dump belongs in a session log, not a comment) and context-first evidence-instruction ordering to exploit provider prompt caching across recovery re-sends.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py — the model-window table (moved from plan_review/sizing.py) + own-window accessor with the conservative unknown-model default.
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py — MODEL_LADDER becomes a re-export of the moved table; largest_window_tokens keeps its escalation semantics unchanged on top of it.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py — two-ceiling bound in _validate_recovery_inputs; the flat _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS constant is replaced by a physical_context_ceiling(model) accessor (window-derived); _validate_recovery_inputs takes the resolved model.
- tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py — its five _cr._MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS references (lines 64, 153, 156, 186, 188) move to the physical_context_ceiling accessor evaluated for the default verifier model; the db1c remedy-wording and 2932-floor assertions keep their semantics against the derived value.
- tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_context_product_bound.py — new held-out oracle for the two ceilings.
- tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py — its _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS references (criteria-budget invariant, oversize refusal) updated to the accessor; constants updated only where they name the old bound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The live c9f7 shape is accepted: _validate_recovery_inputs with a 121,147-char context and 22 criteria under the default claude-sonnet-4-6 resolved model proceeds past preflight, with zero runner calls made before it (unit test, held-out oracle style).
- [ ] The physical ceiling is window-derived: with a haiku-rung resolved model (own window 200,000 tokens) a context over 400,000 chars is refused with CompletionRecoveryError carrying {context_chars, context_char_limit}; with the default claude-sonnet-4-6 model the derived ceiling is 2,000,000 chars (a 400,000-char context is admitted); with an unknown model the ceiling derives from the ladder minimum (unit tests for all three).
- [ ] The own-window accessor returns the matched model's own window, not the escalation max: accessor(haiku rung) = 200,000 while largest_window_tokens(haiku rung) = 1,000,000 remains unchanged for plan-review (unit test pinning both side by side).
- [ ] plan-review call sites are unchanged: existing plan_review sizing tests pass with MODEL_LADDER re-exported (no test edits beyond imports).
- [ ] The economic ceiling holds: a context x criteria product over 3,200,000 is refused with CompletionRecoveryError carrying {context_chars, criteria_total, recovery_input_chars, recovery_input_char_limit} before any runner call (unit test).
- [ ] d59e's pinned invariants stay green: the full context reaches the model byte-identical (nothing elided), _MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS <= the derived context budget still holds, and the over-budget refusal makes zero billable calls (existing d59e tests pass with constants updated only where they name the old bound).
- [ ] Live Bedrock proof before ship: a completion verification whose assembled context exceeds 100,000 chars completes bounded recovery past preflight to a verdict under a forced-low primary budget, instead of refusing at preflight (session experiment, not in unit suite; result recorded on this ticket).
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass; the unit marker suite matches the pre-existing baseline.

## Testing

Held-out unit oracle written RED-first: new tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_context_product_bound.py for the two-ceiling contract (window-derived physical ceiling, unknown-model default, product bound, side-by-side accessor semantics), plus reference updates in test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py and test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py (both consume the physical_context_ceiling accessor in place of the removed constant). Run: python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/ tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py -q and the plan_review sizing tests. Live Bedrock experiment per the live AC recorded as a ticket comment. make lint + make typecheck.
